prior_summary: Destination-frame absolute Cartesian targets retain world tunnel/drawer structure; explicit causal coupling and margin features expose phase, and a narrow closed-near-object guard blocks sampled +x transfer before observed block clearance.
applicable_conditions: Prefer when the block and tunnel are near demonstrated world support and closure/extraction/lift/transfer phase is ambiguous, especially after fingers close. target_pose must be the intended drawer destination and object/TCP/finger observations must be finite.
termination_guidance: After the guard is inactive because the observed object is above 0.16 m, hand off when object and TCP continue together under closed fingers and destination-directed transfer has begun.
limitations: Finger proximity and motion are only grasp proxies. The guard cannot recover a failed grasp, may reject a valid unseen low transfer, and does not ensure collision-free or reachable commands. Destination anchoring is sensitive to large block shifts and unusual entry TCP states.
